title: The Friday Handover Test: Is Your Office Fitout Actually Ready for Monday?
excerpt: A workplace can look finished while the details needed to run the business remain unresolved. Use a handover checklist that tests occupation, systems, furniture and responsibilities before your team arrives.
metaTitle: Office Fitout Handover Checklist: Ready for Monday? | YOS
metaDescription: Check office fitout readiness with a practical handover checklist for approvals, IT, furniture, defects, documentation and staff occupation.
body:
## When is an office fitout ready for occupation?

A fitout is ready when the required occupation conditions are satisfied, essential services and business systems work, and the team can safely use the workplace. A handover date or a finished reception area alone does not establish readiness.

The Friday-to-Monday test is a planning exercise, not a promise that every project can be occupied over a weekend. Ask: if the team arrived next working day, what would stop them doing their jobs?

## Separate project completion from business readiness

Contractual completion, applicable approvals and operational readiness are related but distinct. The project team must establish what each requires for your particular works and building.

A signed handover document does not demonstrate that a video call works, staff access cards are active or delivery packaging has been removed. Those checks need named owners and evidence.

## Build a practical handover register

| Workstream | Readiness check | Evidence to record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approvals and access | Required conditions met; building access agreed | Relevant documents and confirmation from responsible parties |
| Services | Required electrical, mechanical and other systems checked | Testing, commissioning and handover records as applicable |
| IT | Internet, calls and essential business systems tested | Results from realistic user tests |
| Furniture | Installed, stable, set up and clear of access routes | Inspection and supplier actions |
| Defects | Issues recorded and prioritised | Owner, due date and occupation impact |
| Operations | Staff know access, facilities and reporting arrangements | Induction information and contacts |

Identify who has authority to confirm each item. YOS acts as a client-side project manager, coordinating the process; construction, certification and specialist testing remain with the appropriately appointed professionals.

## Test an ordinary working day

Run a small rehearsal rather than checking equipment in isolation. Have a user enter with their access card, connect at a workstation, take a call and join a meeting from the room your team will actually use.

Try the reception and visitor process. Check that furniture placement supports circulation and that storage is usable. Record failures while contractors and suppliers still have clear actions to complete.

## Decide which defects affect occupation

A cosmetic issue and a failed essential system should not sit in the same undifferentiated list. Ask the responsible professionals to identify issues that prevent safe or approved occupation, issues that prevent business operation and issues that can be resolved under an agreed post-handover process.

Do not let a removalist booking determine whether occupation proceeds. Escalate unresolved critical items to the people authorised to assess and decide them.

## Collect the information you will need later

Request the applicable operating instructions, warranties, as-built information, maintenance requirements, test records and supplier contacts. The exact package depends on the scope and contracts, so agree it before the final week.

Make the information accessible to the person managing the workplace. A complete document folder has little value if nobody knows where it is or which maintenance tasks need action.

## Plan the first working week

Name a contact for reporting problems and agree how outstanding actions will be tracked. Coordinate furniture adjustments, IT support and cleaning with the occupation plan.

Distinguish construction-related cleaning from the ongoing office cleaning scope. Confirm who handles remaining dust, packaging and waste so the regular cleaner is not expected to absorb unplanned work.

## Questions business owners ask

### Is a fitout handover the same as permission to occupy?

No. Required approvals and occupation conditions depend on the project and jurisdiction. Confirm them with the relevant professionals rather than relying on the handover date.

### Can minor defects be fixed after staff move in?

Sometimes, subject to professional assessment and the agreed contractual process. Record the work, owner, timing and impact on staff before accepting a post-occupation plan.

### Who should coordinate handover?

A client-side project manager can coordinate the register, dependencies and actions across your appointed team. Each contractor, supplier and certifier remains responsible for their own scope.
